title: Oven Temperature Sensor Open
shortDescription: The oven temperature sensor reads open circuit.
fullDescription:
F1 is posted when the PT500/PT1000 RTD reads infinite resistance. Heating is disabled until the sensor is replaced.

Access is usually at the rear of the cavity behind a retainer plate.

title: Oven Sensor Shorted
fullDescription: F2 is the shorted-sensor counterpart. Replacement is the same as F1; inspect wiring for pinching.

title: Over-temperature
fullDescription:
F3 is posted if the cavity exceeds the max allowed temperature outside self-clean. A welded relay or stuck control is typical.

Turn breaker off and call service.

title: Door Lock Fault
shortDescription: Self-clean door lock did not confirm position.
fullDescription: F4 appears when the lock motor is commanded and the limit switch does not confirm. Lock assembly replacement is usually the fix.
whenToCallPro: If door stuck with hot contents.

faq.a: Yes via control; F4 posts if lock does not return.

title: Door Switch Fault
fullDescription: F5 is posted when the door switch state does not match the lock command. Replace the switch after continuity testing.

title: Cooling Fan Fault
shortDescription: Cooling fan not at target speed.
fullDescription: F6 is raised when the cooling fan tacho is absent or slow. Clean and replace the motor as needed.

title: Meat Probe Fault
fullDescription: F7 is posted when the probe reads open or shorted. Replace probe or clean the jack.

title: Touch Panel Stuck Key
shortDescription: A touch key is reading pressed continuously.
fullDescription: F8 is posted when a key stays active too long. Clean the panel and power cycle.

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: Touch panel and main board not communicating.
fullDescription: F9 indicates lost link between boards. Reseat ribbon after a power cycle.

title: EEPROM / Configuration Fault
fullDescription: F10 signals EEPROM read/write failure. A service-mode reload sometimes works; otherwise replace the control board with one preloaded for the model.

faq.a: User resets do not restore EEPROM.
